channel.title: Daily Teams News summaries
channel.description: Plain-English daily summaries of Microsoft Teams documentation and Message Center changes.

item.title: Teams will retire off-network invitations for Teams Free accounts in December — 10 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 10 November 2026

Teams will retire off-network invitations for Teams Free accounts in December

Starting December 2026, external people will no longer be able to create Teams Free accounts through email invitations or chat links. Existing Teams Free collaboration and federation remain unchanged. The period also updates Teams guidance on external-call limits and Teams Rooms deployment and feature references.

Teams · General

Off-network Teams Free invitations are retiring

Microsoft will retire off-network invitations starting December 2026. Users will no longer be able to invite external people by email or chat link to create Teams Free accounts, while existing Teams Free collaboration and federation continue unchanged.

Teams · General

Teams limits guidance now covers temporary external-call restrictions

The limits documentation now says limits may depend on factors including tenant age and calling activity. When a limit is reached, users may be temporarily unable to place outbound 1:1 calls to external users.

Teams Rooms · AI and Copilot

Teams Rooms Facilitator guidance adds dedicated front-of-room screenshots

The page now uses separate screenshots for the notes panel and Facilitator messages in the chat panel on the front-of-room display, giving administrators clearer visual reference when reviewing these features.

Teams Rooms · General

Teams Rooms Autopilot guidance names version 5.0.111.0

The documentation now identifies version 5.0.111.0 alongside the automatic update functionality included since April 2024, adding a specific version reference for deployment reviews.

View all updates for 10 November 2026 →

item.title: Teams guidance shifts from webinar and town hall names to audience-based event labels — 7 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 7 November 2026

Teams guidance shifts from webinar and town hall names to audience-based event labels

The period is dominated by terminology and procedure updates rather than product rollouts. Updated event guidance now uses “Events up to 1k attendees” and “Events optimized for a large audience” across recording, attendance, setup, captions, publishing, and chat topics. A separate Teams Rooms update revises screenshots and the note-saving workflow.

Teams · Policies and settings

Policy references adopt audience-based event labels

The Settings Policies Reference now uses “Events up to 1k attendees” and “Events optimized for a large audience” instead of webinar and town hall terminology across related settings. Use the revised labels when locating policy controls.

Meetings and events · General

Recording guidance documents separate audience-size event settings

The Meeting Recording article now groups webinars and town halls under events and documents settings for events with up to 1,000 attendees or for large audiences. It also clarifies policy-assignment instructions.

Meetings and events · General

Anonymous-attendance instructions use the new event names

The guide replaces “Who can attend webinars” and “Who can attend town halls” with “Who can attend events up to 1k attendees” and “Who can attend events optimized for a large audience,” and updates the configuration steps for anonymous participants.

Meetings and events · General

Event registration setting receives a new documented name

The setting formerly documented as “Webinar registration form questions” is now called “Events registration form questions.” Administrators should update internal configuration references and runbooks that use the previous name.

Teams Rooms · AI and Copilot

Teams Rooms note-saving workflow and visuals are revised

The Facilitator Teams Rooms article updates screenshots, preview wording, and instructions for adding participant names when saving notes so participants can access notes and transcripts later. The revised workflow is useful for user guidance, with no administrator configuration change stated.

View all updates for 7 November 2026 →

item.title: Teams Rooms app update tool is no longer recommended for new Autopilot deployments — 6 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 6 November 2026

Teams Rooms app update tool is no longer recommended for new Autopilot deployments

This was a quiet, documentation-led day with one actionable Teams Rooms change. The Autopilot guidance says the Teams Rooms app has included automatic updates since April 2024, so the app update tool is no longer recommended for new deployments. A separate known-issues entry records possible Large Gallery unavailability on specified Teams Rooms for Android versions, while release notes document a low-bitrate video fix. Teams Phone updates only reorder language entries in reference and setup material.

Teams Rooms · General

Autopilot guidance changes the app update tool recommendation

Because the Teams Rooms app has included automatic updates since April 2024, the app update tool is no longer recommended for new deployments. Administrators should review Intune configurations and consider unassigning the tool, except when deploying devices older than 2025.

Devices · Troubleshooting

Large Gallery may be unavailable on specified Teams Rooms for Android versions

The known-issues page identifies possible Large Gallery unavailability on Teams Rooms for Android app versions 1449/1.0.96.2026249711 through 1449/1.0.96.2026264504. The issue is expected to be addressed in a future update, and no administrator action is specified.

Teams Rooms · General

Release notes record a low-bitrate video fix

Teams Rooms release notes now document a fix for certain devices sending low-bitrate video in specific meeting scenarios. The supplied evidence states no administrator action.

View all updates for 6 November 2026 →

item.title: Teams will organize muted and meeting chats into dedicated sections in January — 5 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 5 November 2026

Teams will organize muted and meeting chats into dedicated sections in January

Microsoft Teams will introduce a January 2027 chat reorganization: the Muted chats section will be enabled by default, while Meeting chats will be disabled by default, with users able to toggle and reorder both. Two worldwide changes are also planned for December 2026: a Workflows template that links team tags to channel membership and mobile call declines with chat messages. Documentation updates add certified-device entries and SlimCore troubleshooting detail.

Teams · General

Muted and meeting chats get dedicated sections in January 2027

Teams will add Muted chats and Meeting chats sections. Muted chats will be enabled by default, while Meeting chats will be disabled by default. Users can enable or disable and reorder the sections, and muted chats move automatically unless they are favorited. Rollout begins in January 2027, with no admin action required.

Teams · General

Workflows will connect team tags to channel membership

An optional Workflows app template will automatically add users to channels when they are added to a team tag. The feature rolls out worldwide in mid-December 2026 and does not change defaults.

Teams · General

Teams mobile users will be able to decline calls with messages

Users will be able to decline incoming Teams mobile calls with a predefined or custom message sent through Teams chat. Worldwide rollout is scheduled for December 2026; the feature applies only to Teams-to-Teams calls with available chat and requires no admin action.

Devices · General

Certified Hardware Android adds Meeting Owl and Cisco entries

The table now includes Meeting Owl 5 Pro, Owl Tablet, and multiple Cisco devices, along with their associated software versions and certification dates. Administrators can use these details when validating inventories and planning deployments.

Clients · Troubleshooting

SlimCore troubleshooting adds Windows error 6/51 guidance

Vdi 2 Troubleshooting now documents Windows error 6/51, ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE, during SlimCore download, deployment, or startup, and points administrators to BITS Client and AppXDeployment-Server logs.

View all updates for 5 November 2026 →
